defects.observed: After clicking a bar (click.png), the non-selected value labels 5.1M / 4.8M / 6.3M are rendered at opacity 0.32, sampling as RGB(173,173,173) on the RGB(252,252,251) background — a contrast ratio of ~1.95:1. At 17px they are effectively illegible, especially projected.
defects.required: Rubric item 4: text must be legible with sufficient contrast and reasonable presentation font sizes; de-emphasis must not render the data values unreadable.

defects.observed: Selection state can be corrupted by ordinary mouse movement: hideTooltip() unconditionally does valueLabel.classList.remove('dim'), so after clicking Q1 (which dims the other three labels), hovering Q2/Q3/Q4 and moving away permanently restores that label to full opacity while its bar stays dimmed — labels and bars end up in inconsistent highlight states (artifacts/iter3/graph-bar-interactive.html, hideTooltip).
defects.required: Rubric item 11: clicking a bar must produce a consistent, stable highlight state; subsequent hover should not silently undo it.

summary: Core requirements are met and rendered cleanly: exactly four bars with correct proportions (measured heights 167/203/191/251 px vs required 4.2/5.1/4.8/6.3 -> ratios 1.000/1.216/1.144/1.503 against 1.000/1.214/1.143/1.500, <0.3% error), a 0-8M axis with correct gridline placement, all four value labels and Q1-Q4 category labels fully rendered with descenders intact, no overflow (scroll 1280x720), and no console errors. Hover on Q1 shows a '$4.2M' tooltip whose measured bbox is x335-424 / y282-318 against a bar top of y331 — a 13px clear gap, and it overlaps no bar, gridline, tick or label (the bar's own value label is deliberately hidden via visibility, not occluded). Click produces a genuine highlight (darker fill plus 2px stroke, other bars dimmed) and a real summary update reading 'Q1 2025 revenue: $4.2M - highest of the year: no, Q4 is higher at $6.3M.' Two defects hold the score below 85: the dimmed value labels drop to ~1.95:1 contrast and become unreadable in the selected state, and the tooltip's hide handler clears the dim class on any hovered label, so hovering a non-selected bar after a click leaves the highlight state internally inconsistent.
